questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of globalisation?

options.text: Restrictions on expansion of public sector

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberalisation of import licensing**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Liberalisation of import licensing** is a significant feature of globalisation.
 
• Globalisation involves the reduction of trade barriers, allowing for freer movement of goods, services, and capital across borders.
 
• It encourages the integration of national economies into the global economy, enhancing economic cooperation and development.
 
• Other features of globalisation include increased foreign direct investment, technological exchange, and cultural integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalisation** can lead to increased competition, innovation, and access to new markets.
 
• It can also pose challenges such as economic disparity, cultural homogenisation, and environmental concerns.
 
• Governments often implement policies to maximise the benefits of globalisation while mitigating its negative impacts.
 
• International organisations like the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, and the **World Bank** play crucial roles in facilitating global economic cooperation and development.

questions.question: In which of the following ways were farmers encouraged to begin to use high yielding variety seeds?

options.text: Agricultural labourers were paid wages directly by the government.
Farmers’ children were given free education in government colleges and universities.
Farmers were given monetary support in cash to cultivate food grains.
The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Farmers were encouraged to use high yielding variety (HYV) seeds by the government providing seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.
 
• This approach was part of the Green Revolution aimed at increasing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security in India.
 
• The provision of subsidized inputs helped farmers to adopt new technologies and improve crop yields.
 
• Such government initiatives played a crucial role in transforming India's agricultural sector and achieving self-sufficiency in food grain production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution in India started in the 1960s and was a major agricultural reform that introduced new farming techniques and high-yielding crop varieties.
 
• In addition to subsidized inputs, the government also invested in infrastructure such as irrigation, rural roads, and agricultural research and extension services.
 
• The success of the Green Revolution led to increased food grain production, particularly in wheat and rice, and helped India transition from a food-deficient to a food-surplus country.
 
• The initiative had a significant impact on rural incomes and livelihoods, although it also led to regional disparities and environmental challenges.

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct regarding globalization?

I. It involves the creation of networks and activities transcending economic, social and geographical boundaries.

II. Outsourcing is one of the important outcomes of the globalisation process.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​The spread of the flow of** financial products, goods, technology, information, and jobs **across national borders and cultural boundaries is referred to as** globalization**.
 
• In terms of economics, it refers to a** global interdependence** facilitated by **free trade.**
 
• Globalization is a** social, cultural, political, and legal phenomenon**.
 
 
• **Social interaction **between distinct populations increases as a result.
 
• **Cultural interchange** across civilizations is exemplified by globalization in terms of **ideas, values, and artistic expression.**
 
• Another trend associated with globalization is the emergence of a **unified global culture.**
 
• In terms of **politics**, globalization has focused attention on **intergovernmental bodies **such as the **World Trade Organization** and the **United Nations.**
 
• Globalization has changed how **international law is developed **and applied from a **legal perspective.**
 
 
 
• One way that globalization has **boosted the economy and added jobs** is through the **cross-border flow of goods, capital, and labour.**
 
• One of the significant effects of globalization is** outsourcing.**
 
• In outsourcing, a **business engages regular services** from outside vendors, typically **located abroad.**
 
• Companies in **wealthy nations** outsource a lot of services to India, including** voice-based business operations and record guidance.**

• The idea of **five-year plans **is simple- The Government of India prepares a document with all its income and expenditure for five years.
 
• The budget of the central government and all the state governments is divided into two parts: **non-plan budget and plan budget.**
 
• The non-plan budget is spent on routine items yearly. The planned budget is spent on a five-year basis as per the priorities fixed by the plan.
 
• The model of the** Indian Economy **was premised on the concept of planning based on five-year plans from **1951-2017.**
 
• The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the Planning Commission.

questions.question: What is NOT a goal of Five-Year Plans?

options.text: Equal benefits to all the people

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Population Growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian Five-Year Plan :

 
 
• ​A plan spells out how the resources of a nation should be put to use.
 
• It should have some general goals as well as specific objectives which are to be achieved within a specified period of time.
 
• In India, plans are of five years duration and are** called five-year plans** **(we borrowed this from the former Soviet Union, the pioneer in national planning).**
 
• Our plan documents not only specify the objectives to be attained in the five years of a plan but also what is to be achieved over a period of twenty years.
 
• This long-term plan is called a **‘perspective plan’.**
 
• The five-year plans are supposed to provide the basis for the perspective plan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• First Five year Plan (1951- 1956):

 
 
• ​The aim of this plan is to Rehabilitation of refugees, rapid agricultural development to achieve food self-sufficiency in the shortest possible time, and control inflation.
 
• This plan has achieved its Targets and objectives more or less. With an active role of the state in all economic sectors. Five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were started as major technical institutions.
 
 
 
• Second Five year Plan (1956-1961) :
 
 
• ​The aim of this plan is to adopt the Nehru-Mahalanobis model.‘Rapid industrialization with particular emphasis on the development of basic and heavy industries Industrial Policy of 1956 accepted the establishment of a socialistic pattern of society as the goal of economic policy.
 
• However, It could not be implemented fully due to the shortage of foreign exchange. Targets had to be pruned. Yet, Hydroelectric power projects and five steel mills at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established.
 
 
 
• Third Five-year Plan (1961-1966) :
 
 
• ​The aim of this plan is to ‘establishment of a self-reliant and self-generating economy.
 
• However, this plan also becomes a Failure due to Wars and droughts. Yet, Panchayat elections were started.• State electricity boards and state secondary education boards were formed.
 
 
 
• Fourth Five-year Plan (1969-1974) :
 
 
• ​This plan is aiming for ‘growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance Garibi HataoTarget.
 
• But this was also very ambitious so it Failed. Achieved growth of 3.5 per cent but was marred by Inflation. The Indira Gandhi government nationalized 14 major Indian banks and the Green Revolution in India advanced agriculture.
 
 
 
• Fifth Five-year Plan (1974-1979) :
 
 
• ​Then PM Indira Gandhi aimed for the ‘removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance.
 
• The above four five-year plans are aimed at growth only. Now PM Gandhi wanted to remove poverty and inflation in the country. Hence, statement 3) is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four primary explicit goals of five-year plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Education** is not one of the four primary explicit goals of the five-year plans in India.
 
• The four primary explicit goals of the five-year plans are **Growth, Equity, Self-reliance, and Modernization**.
 
• These goals aim to ensure balanced economic growth, reduce inequality, achieve self-sufficiency, and modernize various sectors of the economy.
 
• While education is a crucial aspect of development, it is not explicitly listed as one of the primary goals in the context of five-year plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in **1951** and focused on the agricultural sector.
 
• The concept of Five-Year Plans was inspired by the Soviet model of centralized economic planning.
 
• These plans are formulated, executed, and monitored by the **Planning Commission of India**, which was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in 2015.
 
• Each plan assesses the country's economic situation and sets targets to achieve desired growth and development.
 
• Over the years, the focus of the five-year plans has shifted according to the changing needs and priorities of the country.

questions.question: During one of the Five-Year Plans which of the following politicians gave the slogan ‘Garibi Hatao’?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is** __Indira Gandhi__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The slogan** "Garibi Hatao desh bachao" **was prominently featured in** Indira Gandhi's 1971 election campaign** and later adopted by her son Rajiv Gandhi as well.
 
• In the context of economic planning, **D.D. Dhar's fifth plan **aimed to achieve the "elimination of poverty" (Garibi Hatao) and "attainment of self-reliance" **by promoting rapid economic growth,** **equitable income distribution**, and a **significant increase in domestic savings rates.**
 
• The strategy also prioritized enhancing defence capabilities and achieving agricultural production independence.
 
• However, the concept faced rejection in 1978 under the newly elected** Morarji Desai administration**.
 
• During the period from** 1974 to 1979**, the **Fifth Five-Year Plan** was formulated with objectives centered on boosting employment, reducing poverty, and fostering self-sufficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Charan Singh**, the 5th Prime Minister of India and 5th Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, was deeply involved in the non-violent struggle for India's independence from British rule, following in the footsteps of Mahatma Gandhi. He faced imprisonment multiple times for his activism, including a 12-year jail term in 1930 for violating salt laws.
 
• **Giani Zail Singh,** the seventh President of India, served from July 25, 1982, to July 25, 1987. He actively participated in the Quit India Movement of 1942 and was deeply engaged in the Indian freedom movement, facing incarceration on several occasions for his opposition to British rule.
 
• **Morarji Desai,** the 4th Prime Minister of India (1977-79) and the country's first non-Congress Prime Minister, began his career as a Deputy Collector after graduating from the Wilson Civil Service in Bombay in 1918. Disillusioned with British justice during the Civil Disobedience Movement led by Gandhi in 1930, Desai resigned from government service and joined the struggle for independence.

questions.question: Which Five Year Plan period saw the initiation of the Hill Area Development Programme?

__
 
• The **Hill Area Development Programme** was initiated during the **Fifth Five Year Plan** period in India.
 
• This programme focused on the **development of hilly regions** to ensure balanced regional development and to improve the living conditions of people residing in these areas.
 
• Key objectives included infrastructure development, **agriculture and horticulture enhancement**, and addressing the unique challenges faced by hill areas.
 
• The programme aimed to integrate these regions into the national mainstream, promoting economic growth and social equity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's **Five Year Plans** were a series of centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The **Fifth Five Year Plan** spanned from **1974 to 1978** and aimed at achieving self-reliance and poverty alleviation.
 
• The plan focused on employment, income distribution, and regional balance, along with sectoral growth in agriculture, industry, and services.
 
• Other notable initiatives during this plan included the Minimum Needs Programme and the expansion of the public distribution system.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is correct about MNCs?

**Statements:**

(1) A MNC is a company that owns or controls production in more than one nation.

(2) They lead to creation of monopoly in the home country.

(3) They are also called stateless organisations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements 1 and 3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A multinational corporation( MNC) is a company that operates in its home country, as well as in other countries around the world.
 
• It maintains a central office located in one country, which coordinates the operation of all its other services, similar to executive branches or manufactories.** Hence, Statement 1 is correct.**
 
• It isn’t enough to call a company that exports its products to further than one country a transnational company.
 
• They need to maintain factual business operations in other countries and must make a foreign direct investment there.
 
• In each country, the business may oversee multiple offices that function through several branches and subsidiaries. So, it is called stateless organizations. **Hence, Statement 3 is correct.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Foreign Direct Investment:**

 
 
• 
 
Foreign direct investments are current within transnational pots. Investments do when an investor or company from one country makes an investment outside the country of operation. Foreign investments most frequently do when a foreign business is established or bought outright. It can be distinguished from the purchase of a transnational portfolio that only contains equities of the company, rather than copping more direct control.

questions.question: Which of the following commodities are exempted from GST?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alcohol for human consumption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The new Goods and Services Tax (GST) replaced most of the previous taxes in India.
 
• Now GST will be levied at all stages right from manufacture up to final consumption with credit of taxes paid at previous stages available as setoff.
 
• Only value addition will be taxed and burden of tax is to be borne by the final consumer.
 
• However, at present, following items are kept outside the purview of GST in India:
 
• Alcohol for human consumption:
 
 
• **Alcohol for human consumption has been kept outside the purview of GST in India at present.**
 
• However, the taxes imposed to alcohol for human consumption will continue as per the structure before GST implementation.
 
 
 
• Petroleum products:
 
 
• Petroleum Products such as petroleum crude, motor spirit (petrol), high speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel etc. are also kept outside the purview of GST in India.
 
• Therefore, Petroleum products is kept outside the purview of GST.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body to make recommendations to the Central and State Government on Goods and Services Tax issues.
 
• The GST Council has been provided in Article 279A (1) of the Constitution by the 101st Constitution Amendment.
 
• GST Council is the governing body of GST having 33 members, out of which 2 members are off-center and 31 members are from 28 states and 3 Union territories with legislation.
 
• The GST Council is headed by the Union Finance Minister.

questions.question: The duration of the 12th five year plan was from _______ to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2012 - 2017**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 12th Five Year Plan**, spanning from** 2012 to 2017**, marked the culmination of India's Five Year Plan era.
 
• Despite the challenging global economic climate, Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission, Mr. Montek Singh Ahluwalia, expressed skepticism about achieving an average growth rate of 8% over the subsequent five years.
 
• However, the final growth target of 8% was endorsed during the National Development Council (NDC) meeting in New Delhi.
 
• The Planning Commission aimed to secure NDC approval by September, setting a deadline for the process.
 
• The council was expected to convene after July, contingent upon the Prime Minister's schedule. The primary focus of the plan was on improving health outcomes.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the government opt for a plan holiday after the seventh five - year plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**From 1990 to 1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the conclusion of the **Seventh Five-Year Plan in 1989**, India entered a phase commonly referred to as a** "plan holiday" from 1990 to 1992.**
 
• This period marked a deliberate hiatus in the traditional Five-Year Plans, which had been integral to India's economic planning process since its **independence in 1947**.
 
• The decision to pause the planning cycle was strategic, allowing the government to reassess its economic strategies and priorities without the constraints of adhering to an ongoing plan framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• During the **plan holiday**, India faced significant **economic challenges,** including severe fiscal deficits and imbalances in its balance of payments.
 
• These crises necessitated urgent measures to stabilize the economy and lay the groundwork for sustainable growth.
 
• In response to these challenges, the Indian government initiated far-reaching economic reforms, commonly known as the liberalization reforms of 1991.
 
• These reforms aimed to liberalize and open up the Indian economy, moving away from the centrally planned, state-controlled economic model towards a more market-oriented approach.

questions.question: The adoption of the industrial policy of 1956 coincided with which Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd Five-Year Plan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adoption of the industrial policy of 1956 coincided with the **2nd Five-Year Plan** in India.
 
• The 2nd Five-Year Plan focused on the development of the public sector and rapid industrialization.
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 laid down the framework for the development of industries and aimed at establishing a socialistic pattern of society.
 
• This policy categorized industries into three schedules: those exclusively owned by the state, those progressively state-owned, and those left to private sector development.
 
• It emphasized the role of the public sector in controlling the commanding heights of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **2nd Five-Year Plan** (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model, which gave priority to heavy industries and aimed to build a strong industrial base.
 
• The plan aimed at increasing the national income by 25% and the per capita income by 11%.
 
• The industrial policy of 1956 played a crucial role in shaping India's industrial landscape and promoting balanced regional development.
 
• It was during this plan that significant projects like the Bhilai Steel Plant, Durgapur Steel Plant, and Rourkela Steel Plant were established.

questions.question: A choice of goals has been made in each Plan due to:

__
 
• A choice of goals has been made in each Plan due to the **limitation of resources**.
 
• Resources are not unlimited; hence, prioritization is necessary to allocate them effectively towards the most pressing goals.
 
• This helps in maximizing the impact and ensuring that the most critical areas receive the necessary attention and funding.
 
• Efficient resource management is crucial for sustainable development and achieving long-term objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Resource limitation necessitates careful planning and strategic goal-setting.
 
• Economic plans are often designed with a focus on optimizing the available resources to achieve the best possible outcomes.
 
• Trade-offs are made to balance between various competing needs and priorities.
 
• This approach ensures that the most critical sectors receive adequate resources to drive overall growth and development.

questions.question: Which of the following policy measures is a step towards liberalisation?

options.text: Eliminating licenses for importing a majority of goods
Increasing requirements for bank reserves and restrictions on interest rates

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eliminating Licenses for importing a majority of Goods.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Liberalization** encompasses **the relaxation of state-imposed** constraints across **social, political, and economic spheres**.
 
• It entails a reduction in **government regulations and fosters increased involvement of private entities** in economic activities.
 
• For instance, the elimination of import licenses facilitates greater freedom for businesses, stimulating trade and investment.
 
• **Specific measures **linked with liberalization include the dismantling of excessive government controls on industries, the lowering of trade barriers such as tariffs and interest rates to encourage investment, the promotion of foreign investment across various sectors to attract capital, and the dilution of the public sector's monopoly in different economic segments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advantages of Liberalization**:

 
 
• **Facilitates Free Capital Flow: **Liberalization allows companies to access capital more freely from investors, enabling them to undertake potentially lucrative projects.
 
• **Promotes Higher Growth Rates: **Removal of capital constraints opens up opportunities for profitable ventures, leading to increased economic growth rates.
 
• **Enables Portfolio Diversification:** Investors can diversify their investment portfolios across different asset classes, mitigating risks and maximizing returns.
 
• **Boosts Stock Market Values: **Liberalization measures often lead to increased investor confidence, resulting in higher stock market values and greater trading activity.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Liberalization:**
 
 
• **Redistribution of Economic and Political Power: **Liberalization may lead to a redistribution of economic and political power, potentially concentrating wealth and influence in the hands of a few.
 
• **Increased Competition from MNCs: **Domestic firms, especially smaller enterprises, may face intensified competition from multinational corporations (MNCs), which could threaten their market share and profitability.
 
• **Challenges for Small Companies: **Liberalization can pose challenges for small companies, particularly during mergers or acquisitions with larger corporations, as they may struggle to adapt to new market dynamics and regulatory requirements.

questions.question: The Rolling plan was implemented between which two five-year plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth and Sixth.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Rolling Plan in India was started in 1978__.
 
• The rolling plan concept was coined by** Gunnar Myrdal**.
 
• This plan was rejected again by the Indian National Congress government when it came to power in 1980 and a new sixth plan was made.
 
• The main advantage of the rolling plans is that they are flexible.
 
• The Rolling Plan is a plan in which every year the performance of the plan is assessed and a new plan is made next year based on this assessment.
 
• Thus, both the allocation and targets are revised during this plan.
 
• **In India, the Janta Government terminated the fifth five-year plan in 1977-78 and launched its own sixth five-year plan for the period 1978-83 and called it a Rolling Plan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
 

 Five-year plan
 
 
Time Period

 
 Comment
 
 

 First Plan
 1951-56
 During the initial years of independence, the economy was facing the problem of large-scale foodgrains import (1951) and there was the pressure of price rise. In the plan, the highest priority was given to agriculture including irrigation and power projects. 

 

 
 
 

 Second Plan
 1956-61
 The plan period was 1956–61. The plan laid emphasis on rapid industrialization with a focus on heavy industries and capital goods. The architect of this plan was Professor Mahalanobis. 
 
 

 Third Plan
 1961-65
 This plan incorporated the development of agriculture as one of the objectives of planning in India. It also for the first time, considered the aim of balanced, regional development. Significant events like the war with China in 1961– 62 and with Pakistan in 1965–66 affected the performance of this plan. Also, the severe drought-led famine in 1965–66 led to a heavy drain and diversion of funds, so this plan utterly failed to meet its targets.
 
 

 Three annual plans
 1966-69
 The fourth plan was ready for implementation in 1966- still the government opted for three annual plans due to the weak financial situation and low morale after the defeat by China. Experts, as well as the opposition, called this period as a discontinuity in the planning process. So they named it a period of “Plan Holiday”, i.e., a period when no planning was carried out.
 
 

 Fourth Plan
 1969-74
 The Plan was based on the Gadgil strategy (named after Dhananjay Ramchandra Gadgil, who was a social scientist who had helped in determining the allocation of central assistance for state plans in India.). There was a focus on the ideas of growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance. This plan led to the beginning of the politicisation of planning in India. This led to frequent double-digit inflations, unchecked increases in fiscal deficits etc. Also, there was a first move in the direction of ‘nationalisation’. Greater control and regulation of the economy were some of the salient features of this plan
